problems.title: Count pyramid edges and faces
problems.question: A pyramid has six more edges than faces. Find its edge count.
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: An n-sided pyramid has $E=2n$, $F=n+1$.
steps: 2n−(n+1)=6 gives n=7. Hence E=14.

problems.title: Cancel factorials
problems.question: Simplify (4n)!(n−6)!/[(4n−1)!(n−5)!], for integer n>2022.
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
steps: The first factorial ratio is 4n, and the second is 1/(n−5). Multiply to get 4n/(n−5).

problems.title: A logarithm and the sine bound
problems.question: Solve lg(10^x sin x)>x.
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: The argument must be positive; then $\lg(10^x\sin x)=x+\lg(\sin x)$.
steps: The inequality requires lg(sin x)>0, or sin x>1. This is impossible for a real x.

problems.title: An edge inclination in a square pyramid
problems.question: All eight edges of a regular square pyramid are equal. Find the sine of the angle of a lateral edge to the base.
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: If side length is s, the centre-to-vertex distance is $s/\sqrt2$; $H^2=s^2-s^2/2$.
steps: Thus H=s/√2. The sine is height divided by lateral edge: H/s=1/√2.

problems.title: Combine logarithms with a negative input coefficient
problems.question: Solve log₂(−2x)+log₂(x²)=2.
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: Domain $x<0$; $\log_2u+\log_2v=\log_2(uv)$.
steps: −2x³=4 gives x³=−2, so x=−cube-root(2). It satisfies x<0.

problems.title: Two inclined segments to a plane
problems.question: Two segments from a point to a plane have lengths in ratio 1:2 and projections 1,4. Find the perpendicular height.
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: Pythagoras: $L^2=h^2+p^2$.
steps: The longer projection belongs to the longer segment. Thus h²+16=4(h²+1). This yields h²=4 and h=2.

problems.title: Opposite faces from a cube net
problems.question: In the given net, which listed faces have no common point after folding?
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: Opposite cube faces are disjoint; adjacent faces share an edge.
steps: The net has horizontal row K,N,C; M above C; B below C; A to the right of B.
Fold with C as front: K becomes back, M top, B bottom, N left, A right. Thus A and N are opposite. The other listed pairs share an edge.

problems.title: Recover a set size from its pairs
problems.question: A set has 36 two-element subsets. How many three-element subsets does it have?
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
steps: n(n−1)=72 gives n=9. Hence the triple count is 9×8×7/6=84.

problems.title: Use a median and a unique mode
problems.question: Data are x,y,2,7,9,11; median 6; the only mode is 2. Find the mean.
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: For six sorted observations, median is the mean of the third and fourth.
steps: At least one of x,y must be 2. If both were 2 the middle values would be 2 and 7, giving median 4.5, so exactly one is 2.
The sorted data must be 2,2,t,7,9,11 with (t+7)/2=6, so t=5. The sum is 36 and the mean is 6.

problems.title: Logarithmic inequality with a base below one
problems.question: Solve log₀.₅(x+4)≥1.
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: $0<x+4\le(1/2)^1$ because the logarithm decreases.
steps: Subtract 4 to obtain −4<x≤−3.5.

problems.title: A cone from its sector net
problems.question: A cone has height 12 and lateral net sector angle 72°. Find its lateral area.
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: $2\pi r=(72/360)2\pi l$; $l^2=r^2+h^2$; lateral area $=\pi rl$.
steps: The arc-length condition gives r=l/5. Thus (24/25)l²=144, so l²=150. The lateral area is πl²/5=30π.

problems.title: A sphere through a right triangle
problems.question: A sphere passes through a triangle with sides 6,8,10. Its centre is 2√3 from the triangle plane. Find the sphere radius.
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: The plane-section circle is the triangle’s circumcircle; $R^2=r^2+d^2$.
steps: The triangle is right, with circumradius 10/2=5. Thus sphere radius=√(25+12)=√37.

problems.title: Three parallel lines and a plane
problems.question: Parallel lines a,b,c have pairwise distances ab=13,ac=15,bc=14. Find the distance from a to the plane through b,c.
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: A perpendicular cross-section gives a triangle of sides 13,14,15; Heron area $=\sqrt{s(s-13)(s-14)(s-15)}$.
steps: Its semiperimeter is 21 and area is √(21×8×7×6)=84. The altitude to side 14 is 2×84/14=12, the desired line-to-plane distance.

problems.title: Two possible logarithms in a geometric progression
problems.question: 1−lg x, lg x, 1+lg x form a geometric progression. Which listed interval contains x?
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: Put $t=\lg x$; the middle term squared equals the product of its neighbours.
steps: t²=(1−t)(1+t)=1−t², so t=±1/√2. Both give valid nonzero geometric progressions.
Thus x=10^(−1/√2)≈0.196 or x=10^(1/√2)≈5.095. They lie in (0,3) and (3,6), respectively.
problems.answer: Both listed intervals (0,3) and (3,6) can contain x.
problems.note: The question has two possible answers unless an extra assumption, such as a positive common ratio, is imposed.

problems.title: A line’s angle with a diagonal prism section
problems.question: A regular square prism has height three times its base side. Find the angle between a lateral-face diagonal and a diagonal section.
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: For direction v and plane normal n, $\sin\theta=|v\cdot n|/(|v||n|)$.
steps: Scale the base side to 1. Take v=(1,0,3), and a diagonal plane normal n=(1,−1,0).

problems.title: When does an absolute logarithm have a solution?
problems.question: Find all a for which |log₁₉₉x|=−a²+4a has a positive solution x.
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: The range of $|\log_{199}x|$ on $x>0$ is $[0,\infty)$.
steps: Require −a²+4a=a(4−a)≥0. This gives a∈[0,4]. At either endpoint x=1 is a positive solution.
problems.note: None of the printed choices is correct: (0,4) wrongly excludes the valid endpoints.

problems.title: Evenness includes the domain
problems.question: Which is not even: 3^(|x|−1), (x³−x⁵)/x, [(x−2)(x²+4)]/(x−2), cos(x³)?
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: An even function needs a symmetric domain and $f(-x)=f(x)$.
steps: The first and last are even by absolute value and cosine symmetry. The second simplifies to x²−x⁴ on the symmetric domain x≠0, so is even.
The third simplifies to x²+4 only where x≠2. Its domain contains −2 but not 2, so it is not even.

problems.title: A tilted square between cylinder bases
problems.question: A cylinder has radius 5,height 6. Equal chords AB,CD of its upper and lower bases form square ABCD in a plane not parallel to the axis. Find the square area.
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: A chord of length s is at distance $d=\sqrt{25-s^2/4}$ from its circle centre.
steps: The chord lines are parallel. Equal chords have equal offsets; because the section is tilted, their signed offsets are opposite, so their horizontal separation is 2d.
A square side connecting the bases has length s, with vertical component 6 and horizontal component 2d. Thus s²=36+4d²=36+100−s².
Therefore 2s²=136 and the area s²=68.

problems.title: A union of two finite multiples sets
problems.question: A is the first 100 positive even integers, B the first 50 positive multiples of 3. Find |A∪B|.
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: $|A\cup B|=|A|+|B|-|A\cap B|$.
steps: Common elements are multiples of 6 through 150, so there are 25. The union count is 100+50−25=125.

problems.title: A zero-dot-product locus
problems.question: For fixed distinct A,B in space, describe points C with AC·AB=0.
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: $\overrightarrow{AC}\cdot\overrightarrow{AB}=0$ defines a plane normal to the nonzero vector AB.
steps: The locus is the entire plane through A perpendicular to AB. It includes C=A, since the zero vector also has zero dot product.

problems.title: A rhombus-base pyramid with equal dihedral angles
problems.question: A pyramid base is a rhombus with diagonals 4,6; every lateral face makes 45° with the base. Find height.
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: The apex projection is equidistant from all base-side lines; $H=r\tan45°=r$.
steps: The rhombus area is 4×6/2=12. Each side is √(2²+3²)=√13, so semiperimeter is 2√13.
Equal distances to both pairs of parallel opposite sides force the projection to be the rhombus centre. The inradius is area/semiperimeter=6/√13, also the height.

problems.title: Count walks with unit steps
problems.question: How many sequences a₁,…,a₁₀ have a₁=5 and |aᵢ₊₁−aᵢ|=1?
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: Each of the nine successive steps independently has choices +1 or −1.
steps: There are 2⁹=512 sequences; no other restrictions are given.

problems.title: A logarithmic identity in x
problems.question: Find a+b if 2log₄(x²)+log₂(x+ab) and log₈(x⁶)+log₂3+log₂(ax+1) are identical.
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: $2\log_4x^2=\log_8x^6=2\log_2|x|$ for $x\ne0$.
steps: Cancel the common term. Equality of logarithms gives x+ab=3(ax+1) wherever defined. Equating coefficients yields a=1/3 and ab=3, hence b=9.
These values also give equal domains: x>−3, x≠0. Their sum is 28/3.

problems.title: Three half-lives
problems.question: M(t)=a·1.2^(−kt), a,k>0. Mass falls 50% in 12 hours. What percentage is lost in 36 hours?
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: An exponential has the same multiplicative change over equal time intervals.
steps: Thirty-six hours is three 12-hour intervals. The remaining fraction is (1/2)³=1/8, so the lost fraction is 7/8=87.5%.

problems.title: Angles of a box diagonal to its faces
problems.question: A rectangular box diagonal makes angles x,y,z with its three face directions. Which identity always holds?
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: For edges a,b,c and diagonal $d=\sqrt{a^2+b^2+c^2}$, the line-to-plane sines are $a/d,b/d,c/d$.
steps: Squaring and adding gives (a²+b²+c²)/d²=1.

problems.title: Map one right triangle to another
problems.question: A=(1,1),B=(1,5),C=(3,5); E=(6,1),F=(4,1),G=(4,2). Which transformation types map ABC to EFG?
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: The target sides are half the original sides; AB rotates 90° counterclockwise into EF.
steps: A scale factor 1/2 followed by a 90° counterclockwise rotation, with suitable centres, gives the required direct similarity. A concrete map is (x,y)↦((13−y)/2,(x+1)/2).
It sends A to E, B to F, C to G. Pure translations and rotations preserve size; translation plus homothety alone cannot supply this 90° turn.

problems.title: Minimize a trigonometric quotient
problems.question: Find the minimum of (2−sin²x)/(2−cos²x).
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: Put $t=\sin^2x\in[0,1]$; the quotient is $(2-t)/(1+t)$.
steps: Its derivative in t is −3/(1+t)²<0, so it is smallest at t=1. The minimum is 1/2, attained when x=π/2+kπ.

problems.title: Separate two filling rates
problems.question: Two pipes together fill a tank in 3 hours; the first alone in 4 hours. How long for the second alone?
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
steps: 1/T=1/12, so T=12 hours.

problems.title: A cylinder section parallel to the axis
problems.question: A cylinder has radius 5,height 6. A plane parallel to its axis is 2 from the axis. Find section area.
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: The rectangular section has width $2\sqrt{R^2-d^2}$ and height H.
steps: The width is 2√21 and the area is 6×2√21=12√21.

problems.title: An oblique chord through a diameter endpoint
problems.question: A radius-2 circle has diameter AB. D is beyond B with BD=3; ED⊥AD and ED=5. AE meets the circle again at C. Find area ABC.
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
steps: Line AE is y=5x/7. Substitute into the circle: (74/49)x²=4x. The second intersection has x=98/37, y=70/37.
Triangle ABC has base 4 and height 70/37, so area=140/37. Reflection of E across AB gives the same area.

problems.title: Count teams with exactly one of each name
problems.question: A class has 4 Giorgis and 3 Ninos. Exactly one Giorgi and one Nino must be in each four-student team; there are 936 such teams. Find class size.
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: If m students have neither name, team count $=4\cdot3\binom m2$.

problems.title: The largest triangular section of a cone
problems.question: A cone has height 10. The maximum area of a section through two generators is twice its axial-section area. Find generator length.
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: For angle θ between generators, area $=l^2\sin\theta/2$; axial area $=rh$.
steps: If r<h, the apex angle is below 90°, so the axial section is already maximal; it cannot have half the maximum area. Thus r≥h, and a 90° pair of generators exists, giving maximum l²/2.
Set l²/2=2rh and use l²=r²+h². Then (r/h)²−4(r/h)+1=0, so r/h=2±√3. Only 2+√3 meets r≥h.

problems.title: Solve a radical-logarithm system
problems.question: Solve √y+lg(x²)=2, y+4lg x=28.
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: The second logarithm requires $x>0$; put $t=\sqrt y\ge0$, $u=\lg x$.
steps: The equations are t+2u=2 and t²+4u=28. Eliminate u to obtain t²−2t−24=0, giving t=6 or −4.
Keep t=6, so y=36 and u=−2. Thus x=0.01. Direct substitution gives 6−4=2 and 36−8=28.

problems.title: Project a section of an equal-edge pyramid
problems.question: MABC has C=90° and MA=MB=MC. K on MB has MK:KB=2:3. Area ACK=25, cos of angle between ACK and ABC is 0.6, and pyramid volume is 1. Find its height.
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: Projected area $=S\cos\alpha$; volume $=S_{ABC}H/3$.
steps: The apex projection O is the circumcentre of right triangle ABC, hence the midpoint of AB. Since K=(3M+2B)/5, its projection is K₀=(3O+2B)/5=(3A+7B)/10.
Thus K₀ is 7/10 of the way from A to B, so area ACK₀=(7/10)area ABC. The projected section area is 25×0.6=15.
Therefore area ABC=150/7. From volume 1, H=3/(150/7)=7/50.

problems.title: Count logarithmic ordered pairs
problems.question: Count positive real a and integers b∈[2,200] satisfying (log_b a)^2023=log_b(a^2023).
problems.idea: Translate the statement into an equation and check its domain and geometry.
formulas: Put $t=\log_ba$; then $t^{2023}=2023t$.
steps: The real solutions are t=0 or t²⁰²²=2023, giving exactly three values: 0 and ±2023^(1/2022).
For each of the 199 possible bases b, exponentiation a=b^t gives three distinct positive a values. Hence there are 199×3=597 ordered pairs.
